item.title: Entergy suspends disconnects through August 21 amid extreme heat wave
item.dc:creator: Shelli Poole
item.description: Entergy Arkansas has announced a temporary suspension of residential service disconnections for all customers through Friday, August 21, to protect public safety during a period of extreme heat. The utility provider confirmed that disconnection procedures will not resume until Monday, August 24, as dangerous temperatures continue to impact communities across the state. Read more below. […]
item.content:encoded:
Entergy Arkansas has announced a temporary suspension of residential service disconnections for all customers through Friday, August 21, to protect public safety during a period of extreme heat. The utility provider confirmed that disconnection procedures will not resume until Monday, August 24, as dangerous temperatures continue to impact communities across the state. Read more below.




The temporary suspension is a proactive safety measure intended to help residents keep their cooling systems running during the ongoing heat wave. Company officials noted that while they are pausing disconnections, this does not prevent the possibility of unexpected power outages caused by severe weather, emergencies, or equipment damage.

In addition to suspending shutoffs, Entergy Arkansas has issued a set of critical guidelines to help customers manage their energy usage and avoid heat-related health emergencies. Cooling costs typically represent the largest portion of a household’s electric bill during the summer, but several low-cost or no-cost strategies can significantly reduce energy consumption:

  • Adjust the thermostat:
    Residents are advised to set their thermostats to the highest temperature that remains comfortable.
  • Maintain air-conditioning units:
    Routinely cleaning or replacing air filters helps systems run more efficiently.
  • Utilize fans:
    Ceiling and portable fans can effectively circulate cool air, though they should be turned off when rooms are unoccupied.
  • Block sunlight:
    Closing blinds, curtains, and shades during the hottest afternoon hours helps keep indoor temperatures down.
  • Seal air leaks:
    Gaps around doors, windows, and ductwork should be sealed to keep conditioned air from escaping.

Entergy Arkansas offers energy-monitoring resources through its online portal, where customers can use myAdvisor tools to track real-time energy use and identify custom savings options. Additional energy-efficiency programs, rebates, and bill-assistance tools are available through the company’s online Bill Toolkit.

For those working outdoors, safety remains paramount. Health experts advise drinking plenty of water, scheduling strenuous labor during the coolest times of the day, and taking frequent breaks in shaded or air-conditioned areas. Signs of heat exhaustion include heavy sweating, headache, nausea, and extreme fatigue. If an individual shows signs of heat stroke—such as confusion, seizures, hot and dry skin, or loss of consciousness—emergency services should be contacted immediately.

For additional energy-saving, bill-management and customer assistance resources, visit Entergy Arkansas.

item.content:encoded:
If you would like to have a full obituary published with pictures, click here to get started: www.mysaline.com/submit-obits

Billy Gene Coker

Billy Gene Coker, 89, of Perryville, passed away peacefully in his home on August 11, surrounded by the life and love he built over nearly nine decades. 

Born in Conway, Billy was the son of Alvis Coker and Amy Gunter (née Heffington). He was preceded in death by his parents; brothers, Bobby Coker, James Mahan, Larry Mahan, and Sandy Coker; and sisters, Alva Dean Coker, Carolyn Nagel, and Linda Coker. 

Billy was the beloved partner of Debbie Tate for 36 years and a devoted father to Caryn Burge and her husband, Jason, and Danny Coker and his wife, Tonya. He was a proud grandfather to Sara Coker, Jenna Coker, Jayme Denker, and Kaila Collins, and a loving great-grandfather to Reed Collins. 

Billy loved his family deeply and found joy in the simple things in life. He was an avid outdoorsman who loved hunting and fishing, spending time with the people he loved, and, of course, tossing back a few “cold ones.” 

Those who knew Billy will remember the life he lived, the stories he shared, and the love he had for his family. After 89 years, he leaves behind a lifetime of memories that will continue to be told, laughed about, and cherished by those who loved him most. 

He will be deeply missed and forever loved.

Visitation will be 1:30 to 2:00 p.m. Friday, August 14 at Ashby Funeral Home with his Celebration of Life to begin at 2:00 p.m.

Yvonne Lynn Martin-Caple

Yvonne Lynn Martin-Caple, 63, of Benton, Arkansas, passed away August 11, 2026. She was born February 16, 1963, in Charleston, South Carolina, to Emory L. Martin, Sr. and Hazel (Hobby) Martin.

Yvonne worked for many years in food service at the Arkansas Health Center. She was an incredible baker, and those who knew her best were fortunate enough to enjoy the sweet treats she made with her special ingredient, love. Her family especially looked forward to her Neiman Marcus brownies, fudge, dirt cake, and no-bake cookies. Whatever she made, it was always better because it came from Yvonne’s kitchen.

Anyone who stepped inside Yvonne’s home quickly discovered another thing she loved—angels. Her family often gave them to her as gifts, and over the years, she collected enough to have them displayed throughout her home. Each one was special, and together they became a beautiful reflection of something that brought her great joy.

Yvonne also had a love for flowers and plants and enjoyed spending time outdoors. She liked camping, although her version of camping was definitely more “glamping”—and air conditioning was not optional! She appreciated the beauty of the outdoors while still enjoying the comforts of home.

Above all, Yvonne treasured her family. Holidays, birthdays, and family gatherings were some of her favorite times because they meant being surrounded by the people she loved. She found happiness in the simple things—something sweet from the kitchen, beautiful flowers, time outside, and a house filled with family.

Yvonne was preceded in death by her parents, Emory L. Martin, Sr. and Hazel (Hobby) Martin; brother, Gary L. Martin; and two nephews.

She leaves behind to cherish her memory her loving husband of 38 years, Dennis Caple; sons, Jeffery Caple and wife Rebekah, and Jody Caple; sisters, Debra Stephens and husband Kevin, and Teresa Witham and husband Lance; brothers, Emory L. Martin, Jr. and wife Diana, Richard Martin and wife Nicole, Michael Martin, Jason Martin and wife Naomi, and Timothy Martin and wife Missy; 28 nieces and nephews; numerous great-nieces and great-nephews; and many cousins, extended family members, and friends who loved Yvonne and will miss her always.

Visitation will be held from 5:00–7:00 PM, Monday, August 17, at Smith-Benton Funeral Home, 322 N. Market Street in Benton, Arkansas.

Funeral service, officiated by Bro. Kirby Caple, will be held at 2:00 PM, Tuesday, August 18, at Smith-Benton Funeral Home. Burial will follow at McPherson Cemetery in Sardis, with Roger Fagan, Josh Holmes, Blake Narramore, Lance Witham, Phillip Koch, and Charles Caple assisting as pallbearers.

Yvonne leaves behind more than the things she loved and the treats everyone looked forward to—she leaves behind a lifetime of memories made with the people who mattered most to her. Her family will remember her in every gathering, every blooming flower, every favorite dessert, and perhaps even every camping trip made just a little more comfortable with some good air conditioning.

item.dc:creator: Shelli Poole
item.description: The Saline County Fair Association is hosting its fourth Flea Market and Trade Day on Saturday, August 15, offering a diverse array of local merchandise, crafts, and food. Proceeds from this free event will directly fund ongoing efforts to rebuild and improve the Saline County Fairgrounds. Read more below. The community fundraiser, themed “Rebuilding Together,” […]
item.content:encoded:
The Saline County Fair Association is hosting its fourth Flea Market and Trade Day on Saturday, August 15, offering a diverse array of local merchandise, crafts, and food.

Proceeds from this free event will directly fund ongoing efforts to rebuild and improve the Saline County Fairgrounds. Read more below.




The community fundraiser, themed “Rebuilding Together,” is 7:00 a.m. to 2:00 p.m. at the Fairgrounds, at 406 Fairfield in Benton. The event will take place rain or shine, because the indoor vendor buildings are fully air-conditioned.

Shoppers can expect to find a wide variety of goods, including:

  • yard sale items,
  • flea market finds,
  • crafts,
  • antiques,
  • fresh produce,
  • eggs,
  • animals, and
  • animal supplies.

Come hungry,  because the Homemakers Extension kitchen and concession stand will be open, serving a variety of foods and treats to raise additional funds for the rebuilding project.

If you’d like to be a vendor, indoor and outdoor vendor spaces are still available. A 12×12-foot outside space costs $25, while a 10×10-foot inside space is $50. The spaces do not include tents, tables, chairs, electricity, or water, and all booth rental proceeds go directly toward the fairgrounds.

Vendor setup is scheduled for Friday evening from 4:30-7:00 p.m., and Saturday morning at 6:00 a.m. Participating businesses are required to meet all standard licensing requirements, and animal vendors must comply with applicable regulations.

Upcoming Flea Market and Trade Days are scheduled for September 26, October 24, and a two-day event on November 6 and 7. Interested vendors or attendees can request  information by texting 501-860-3101, emailing salinecofair@hotmail.com, or visiting the association’s online registration form.

item.title: Police narrative reveals murder victim from Saline County recorded his own death on cell phone
item.dc:creator: Shelli Poole
item.description: UPDATE AUG 12, 2026 EARLIER: JUL 15, 2026 Chilling details have emerged in the capital murder case with suspects Yudith Cicard Reyes and Luis Felipe Reyes-Isabel of Saline County, Arkansas. Court records reveal that the victim, Jose Miguel Quiroz-Mata, recorded his own fatal shooting on his cell phone. Read more below. Quiroz-Mata, age 44, was […]
item.content:encoded:
UPDATE AUG 12, 2026
EARLIER: JUL 15, 2026

Chilling details have emerged in the capital murder case with suspects Yudith Cicard Reyes and Luis Felipe Reyes-Isabel of Saline County, Arkansas. Court records reveal that the victim, Jose Miguel Quiroz-Mata, recorded his own fatal shooting on his cell phone. Read more below.




Quiroz-Mata, age 44, was found dead inside his vehicle in Little Rock on July 14, 2026, just days after he had repeatedly contacted law enforcement to report a suspected arson, escalating threats, and the physical sabotage of his vehicle.

According to an arrest affidavit from the Little Rock Police Department, officers responded to a ShotSpotter alert and subsequent shooting call at approximately 6:09 a.m. on July 14, 2026, in the 4200 block of W. 10th St.

Upon arrival, first responders located Quiroz-Mata deceased in the driver’s seat of his white Chevrolet, suffering from multiple gunshot wounds. Processing of the crime scene yielded three .380-caliber cartridge casings, shattered glass, and a projectile strike on the driver’s side door frame.

Yudith Cicard Reyes • Arrest Date: 07/14/2026 • Agency: Little Rock Police Department • Age: 49 • White Female • DOB: 05/06/1977 • Charged with: #1 warrant: affidavit-felony warrant issued by little rock police department, ar; #2 CAPITAL MURDER • NO BOND.
Luis Reyes • Arrest Date: 07/14/2026 • Agency: Little Rock Police Department • Age:22 • White Male • DOB: 10/20/2003 • Charged with: #1 warrant: affidavit-felony warrant issued by ar. NO BOND, ICE PENDING.


The breakthrough in the investigation came when detectives discovered Quiroz-Mata’s cell phone on the driver-side floorboard of his vehicle. After obtaining the passcode from family members, detectives discovered a video recording captured by the victim immediately prior to his death.

The footage captured a black truck blocking the roadway, followed by a male identified as 22-year-old Luis Felipe Reyes-Isabel approaching the victim’s vehicle with a handgun and firing five rounds inside.

Witnesses in the neighborhood reported hearing five gunshots, seeing a black truck follow a white truck, and hearing screams. One witness told detectives they specifically observed Quiroz-Mata’s ex-wife, 49-year-old Yudith Reyes, sitting in the front passenger seat of the suspect vehicle during the shooting.

Additionally, a resident’s security camera captured footage of Quiroz-Mata’s white Chevy striking a mailbox at 6:08 a.m., with the black truck trailing slowly behind it.

Using Flock license plate readers, investigators tracked the movements of a black 2026 Dodge Ram registered to Yudith Reyes. The vehicle was recorded northbound on Chicot Road at 3:30 a.m. and southbound on Cedar Street at 3:51 a.m. City surveillance cameras also captured both Yudith Reyes and Reyes-Isabel riding in the truck together on Geyer Springs Road at 6:18 a.m., minutes after the shooting.

Later that morning, detectives spotted Yudith Reyes’s second vehicle, a Chevrolet Trailblazer, at an office strip at the 10600 of Colonel Glenn Road, and took her into custody without incident.

Investigators subsequently executed a search-and-seizure warrant at her home located in the Royal Oaks neighborhood in Mabelvale. Inside the residence, police recovered a Ruger .380-caliber gun box, a paycheck stub for Reyes-Isabel, and his state fisheries conservation license.

After being read her Miranda rights, Yudith Reyes provided a recorded statement admitting that Reyes-Isabel drove the truck to the crime scene, shot Quiroz-Mata, and fled.

Although she initially claimed Reyes-Isabel was her cousin, family members refuted that assertion to police. Both suspects are currently being held without bond at the Pulaski County Regional Jail on charges of capital murder. Mr. Reyes-Isabel has a case pending with Immigration & Customs Enforcement (ICE).

The arrest affidavit also reveals that Mr. Quiroz-Mata had spent weeks pleading with authorities for assistance as the situation escalated. On June 15, 2026, he reported to police that his ex-wife may have been responsible for a house fire.

On July 9, he filed a formal harassment complaint at the prosecuting attorney’s office. Finally, on July 12 — just 48 hours before he was killed — Quiroz-Mata filed a police report stating that Reyes’s boyfriend had physically sabotaged his vehicle.

item.content:encoded:

Raymond Wendall Wilbanks

Raymond Wendall Wilbanks, age 65, of Benton passed away on Monday, August 10, 2026. He was born March 11, 1961 in DeQueen, Arkansas.

Wendall was a loving husband, father, grandfather, son, brother, and friend. Anyone who knew Wendall knew how much he loved spending time with his family. His greatest joy was being with his grandchildren and making memories with the people he loved. In his younger years, Wendall could often be found working on cars, a hobby he enjoyed throughout his life.

He is survived by his beloved wife, Jamie Wilbanks; his children, Mary McConihay (Travis), Kristin Griffin (Mark), Corey Skinner (Megan), and Wendall Wilbanks; and his grandchildren, Cole, Aubree, Kaydence, Anna, Hadley, and Joshua. He is also survived by his parents, Jo Ann and Robert Wilbanks; and his siblings, Ramona Weiss and Richard Wilbanks.

Wendall was preceded in death by his siblings, Rose Marie Wilbanks, Ronald Wayne Wilbanks, Robert Lynn Wilbanks, and Rhonda Jo Price.

Wendall will be deeply missed by his family and all who knew and loved him. His love for his family, his devotion to his grandchildren, and the memories he created with those around him will remain in their hearts forever.

Visitation will be held Friday, August 14, 2026, from 9:00 to 10:00 a.m. at Ashby Funeral Home in Benton, Arkansas. Funeral services will follow, with Pastor Mark Blakely officiating. Burial will follow the service at FairPlay Cemetery in Glen Rose, Arkansas.

item.content:encoded:

Jeffery Alan Ramsey

After more than four decades of serving his state, protecting his community, and standing beside countless people in their time of need, Senior Corporal Jeffery Alan Ramsey’s watch ended on August 7, 2026.

Born October 28, 1960, in Benton, Arkansas, Jeff was the son of Bill and Sarah Ramsey. His career in law enforcement began with the Saline County Sheriff’s Office before he went on to serve 33½ years with the Arkansas State Police. Known by his call sign A81, Jeff wore the badge with pride and earned the respect of those who worked alongside him and those he served. After retiring from the State Police, he continued serving his community as Chief of Police in Haskell for a year and a half.

Jeff was a protector by nature and someone others knew they could count on. He took his responsibilities seriously and was a mentor to many young officers, teaching not only the job, but what it meant to be a good cop. Beneath his strong presence was a generous heart, a sense of humor, fierce loyalty, and a genuine concern for others. His brothers in blue became an important part of his life, and the friendships he formed through his years of service remained long after assignments changed.

Above all, Jeff took great pride in being a father. His children meant the world to him, and he did not take the privilege of being their father lightly. He was devoted to his mother, siblings, adopted children, extended family, and close friends, always making sure the people he loved knew they mattered.

Jeff loved the Lord and was a faithful member of Spring Creek Baptist Church, where he especially enjoyed his Men’s Bible Study and Sunday School class. He spoke openly about his relationship with Jesus and was at peace with the promise of Heaven.

Away from the badge, Jeff enjoyed Conway Twitty and Alan Jackson, keeping his lawn (and sometimes his neighbors’ lawns) mowed, cheering on the Razorbacks with pizza from Larry’s Pizza in Haskell, and spending time at the casinos. He also had a bucket list he was working his way through, and the only thing he didn’t get to cross off was trying out the new Buc-ee’s. Jeff loved him some Buc-ee’s.

Jeff is survived by his children, Morgan Ramsey and J. Alan Ramsey; his mother, Sarah Ramsey; siblings, Rocky (Gina) Ramsey, Robin (Gary) Ramsey Pelton, and Michael (Sherry) Ramsey; adopted children, Sarah, Ashley, and Tim Tate; and many nieces, nephews, cousins, extended family members, and close friends. He will also be deeply missed by his brothers in blue, and by the many people whose lives were touched by him.

He is now reunited in eternity with his father, Bill Ramsey; and grandparents, C.R. and Lottie Bell Statler and James and Willie Mae Ramsey.

Visitation will be held from 5:00 to 7:00 p.m. Thursday, August 13, 2026, at Smith Benton Funeral Home, 322 N. Market St., Benton. Funeral services will be held at 10:00 a.m. Friday, August 14, 2026, at Spring Creek Baptist Church, 19200 I-30 Frontage Rd., Benton. Burial will follow at Mt. Harmony Cemetery.

Pallbearers are J. Alan Ramsey, Gary Adams, Ryan Jacks, Greg Church, Tyler Hamilton, and Evan Williams. Honorary pallbearers are Will Bearden, Michael Ramsey, Rocky Ramsey, and Brandon Blaylock.

In lieu of flowers, memorials may be made to CARTI, the Arkansas State Police Foundation, or Spring Creek Baptist Church.

The family extends their heartfelt gratitude to the doctors, nurses, and staff who cared for Jeff, especially the ECMO team at UAMS. Their skill, compassion, and dedication throughout his care will never be forgotten.

Jeff’s watch may have ended on August 7th, but the impact on the lives he touched and the example he left behind will remain.

item.content:encoded:
Join Saline County History & Heritage Society (SCHHS) for the 40th anniversary celebration on August 13th. Read more below.




Come to commemorate the inception of the SCHHS back in 1986 as a nonprofit – preserving, researching, and exploring the history and heritage of our Saline County community.

The fun is on Thursday, August 13. The program begins at 5:00 p.m. at 123 North Market St.

Show your support for history by attending this presentation, and bring a friend. There’s no charge to attend, and guests are welcome.

However, if you’d like to become a supporting member of the SCHHS, it’s $25 per year per household which helps to sustain our non-profit in educating the community on the county’s history, preservation of our great heritage, and providing a space for research.

item.title: Arkansas Governor to appoint temporary replacement for recovering Justice Barbara Webb

The request, made in a letter on Monday, comes as Webb’s family anticipates her potential return […]
item.content:encoded:
Above: Justice Barbara Webb. Photo courtesy of Arkansas Judiciary.

Arkansas Supreme Court Chief Justice Karen Baker has formally requested that Gov. Sarah Huckabee Sanders appoint a temporary special justice to fill the seat of Associate Justice Barbara Webb, of Benton, Arkansas, who is recovering from a head injury.

The request, made in a letter on Monday, comes as Webb’s family anticipates her potential return for the court’s fall term but seeks a temporary replacement to ensure the court remains at its full constitutional capacity during her recovery. Read more below.




In May, Justice Webb sustained a head injury following a fall at her home while doing laundry late in the evening, according to her husband Doyle Webb. She has since been undergoing treatment for the injury at a medical facility in Houston, Texas.

According to her husband, Doyle Webb, she is scheduled to return to Little Rock to undergo one additional surgery at UAMS, which will be followed by an unspecified recovery period. Doyle Webb stated that he advised Chief Justice Baker of his wife’s condition, noting that while Justice Webb anticipates returning to her duties in time for the Supreme Court’s fall term, they requested a temporary replacement in the event her recovery requires more time than currently expected.

In her letter to Governor Sanders on Monday, August 10, 2026, Chief Justice Baker formally certified that Justice Webb is temporarily unable to perform her judicial duties. Rather than requesting that a separate special justice be appointed for each individual case during her absence, Baker requested the appointment of a single temporary special justice who can handle all of Webb’s duties until she is able to resume them.

Under Amendment 80, Section 13(A) of the Arkansas Constitution, if a Supreme Court Justice is temporarily unable to serve, the Chief Justice certifies this to the Governor, who then has 30 days to commission a Special Justice. The temporary appointment will expire as soon as Webb notifies the Supreme Court that she is ready and able to return.

Under state constitutional requirements, the Arkansas Supreme Court must be composed of seven justices to function at full capacity. The transition to a temporary replacement ensures that the court will avoid potential delays or split decisions in upcoming cases during the transition period.
